title: Claude's $31K Trading Loss, Slack Turns Coding Into a Team Sport, and the AI Router Gold Rush
tldr: A Reddit user says an unsupervised Claude trading agent lost him $31,000 in a month — a live warning shot for anyone piloting agentic finance.
Slack launched "Slack Code," letting AI agents and human teammates build software together inside shared channels.
AT&T cut AI costs up to 90% by routing routine work to cheaper open models, fueling a router acquisition wave (Stripe's $7B OpenRouter buy, Ramp's new Router tool).

tips.heading: Turn a chat into a live website with ChatGPT Sites
steps: In ChatGPT, mention @Sites or include the word "website" in your request.
Describe the audience, the job the site should do, and its features — ask it to save a reviewable version first, since deploy URLs go live instantly.
Once it looks right, ask Sites to deploy it and hand you the production URL.
tips.prompt: Build a website for [audience] that helps them [job]. Include [sections/features]. Save a reviewable version before deploying. Once I approve it, publish it with Sites and give me the live URL.

tips.heading: Package your AI know-how into a paid workflow audit
steps: Have Claude interview you on your strongest industries and tools, then suggest three consulting angles.
Build a short AI assessment for a prospect that scores where AI could help their business, published as a live Artifact.
Feed Claude their answers plus their website and ask it to find the highest-return bottleneck to fix with AI.
Have it turn the findings into a client-ready slide deck: the result, the bottleneck, a solution, and a next step.

news.body: AT&T cut AI costs up to 90% by routing routine work to cheaper open models. It now sends 40% of employee AI use to open models; a router acquisition wave followed, including Stripe's $7B buy of OpenRouter.
news.means: Model routing is a real budget lever, not a novelty — worth raising with clients overpaying for work a cheaper model could handle.

news.body: Slack launched "Slack Code," letting AI agents and teammates build software together inside shared channels. Agents like ChatGPT, Claude, and Devin can join, write code with live previews, and hand off changes for human approval.
news.means: A preview of where team tools are heading — worth watching if clients live in Slack, since it lets non-engineers direct agentic coding work.

news.body: A Reddit user says an unsupervised Claude trading agent lost him $31,000 in a month. He's warning agents shouldn't control real money unsupervised — though others question if the screenshot is genuine.
news.means: Authenticity aside: any client piloting agentic finance should paper-trade first, cap position sizes, and set a hard stop.

beyond_ai.body: North Korea fired about 10 short-range ballistic missiles into its eastern waters, hours after dismissing President Trump's latest push to ease tensions. The test came during US-South Korea military drills that Trump shortened from 11 to 5 days; Kim Jong Un's sister called the reduction meaningless, and Trump says he hopes to meet Kim again this year.
beyond_ai.angle: No direct relevance to your work, general awareness only.
beyond_ai.starter: Trump wants another Kim summit right after North Korea test-fired missiles during the drills he just shortened — anyone else find that timing wild?

beyond_ai.body: Walmart posted its slowest US sales growth in almost six years (2.6%), and shares dropped over 9%. The CFO cited a softening consumer and $4-plus gas prices; Walmart is plowing a record $2.9B tariff refund into cutting prices on 11,000 items.
beyond_ai.angle: A live signal that consumer spending is cooling — useful context if you're advising retail or CPG clients on Q4 pricing and promotion plans.
beyond_ai.starter: Walmart just posted its slowest sales growth in six years — are we seeing that same softening with any of our retail clients?

beyond_ai.body: A Chinese court sentenced Evergrande founder Hui Ka Yan to life in prison for fraud tied to the company's 2021 collapse. The developer defaulted on more than $300B in debt after overstating revenue by roughly $80B; China's housing crisis has since erased about $18T in household wealth.
beyond_ai.angle: No direct relevance to your work, general awareness only.
beyond_ai.starter: Evergrande's founder just got a life sentence — wild that a $300B default is still working its way through China's economy five years later.

beyond_ai.body: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent doubled the bond buyback program to at least $4B per operation after 30-year yields hit 5.32%, their highest since 2007. Yields dipped briefly on the news before rebounding; analysts say buybacks don't fix the underlying reasons investors are demanding higher premiums on US debt.
beyond_ai.angle: Borrowing costs are the through-line in every client budgeting conversation right now — this is the same story as this week's $40T debt milestone, just getting sharper.
beyond_ai.starter: 30-year yields just hit their highest since 2007 — is anyone still planning around cheap long-term financing?

beyond_ai.body: Charter Communications completed its $34.5B acquisition of Cox Communications, creating a combined cable operator serving about 37 million subscribers across 45 states.
beyond_ai.angle: A useful consolidation data point if any clients operate in telecom, media, or adjacent markets watching for pricing and bundling shifts.
beyond_ai.starter: Charter just closed a $34.5B deal for Cox — curious whether that changes any of our clients' negotiating leverage with cable/internet providers.
